items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And I also did an album with Basie for Kay Starr, who was a surprisingly hip singer

ctx.x: Yeah. Then some time went by and I did some other things which I think were more successful. The Mills Brothers album, “Chairman of the Board,” and was there as second one, I can’t quite remember whether I did one or maybe two of them. But that was really great because that was taking things that the Mills Brothers and Basie had done and just making them fit together. And I enjoyed that. And I also did an album with Basie for Kay Starr, who was a surprisingly hip singer and it was a surprisingly good album. I…
Some of our younger viewers might not remember the Arthur Godfrey Show, but did you have some experiences in there that were new? It must have been that every week something would come along.
